name: webhook-delivery-latency
title: Mitigate webhook delivery latency
description: Reduce the finite (minutes-scale) webhook delivery latency: a message visible in the Telegram client is not observed as an inbound POST by the same-host receiver until minutes later. Producer-side: bound per-endpoint delivery latency (bounded per-endpoint concurrency, measured-based delivery timeout, latency observability) and settle the delivery loss policy (best-effort in-memory vs durable outbox). The webhook receiver is a black box; fast-ack and idempotent-ingest are receiver-side contracts. This task lands research + design first; implementation is a later phase.
scope: producer side only; receiver is a black box (fast-ack + idempotent-ingest are required-of contracts, not implemented); TWO PROBLEMS: (P1) the 10-minute total-silence window (zero requests, text+media) is COUPLED TO THE OFFICIAL CLIENT NOT HAVING THE CHAT OPEN (client + Budva are separate sessions; channels/supergroups [any size — no protocol threshold] not guaranteed real-time) — leading causal class = open-chat-triggered update acquisition (B1a-B1d, incl. documented cross-session passive-update for accessible non-member channels/supergroups), localized by a one-shot owner-run BOUNDARY-LOCALIZATION EXPERIMENT + one live SIGQUIT dump + the owner-supplied SOURCE CHAT TYPE (NOT endpoint HOL, capped <=60 s at timeoutSeconds:60); fix direction = make Budva an active subscriber (OpenChat, native, pending experiment); (P2) steady-state per-message delay = native Go in internal/service/push (bounded per-endpoint concurrency + test-justified timeoutSeconds + post-deploy queue-depth/oldest-age metrics); evidence for P2 = a controlled slow-receiver test (NOT production timing collection; P1 boundary experiment is the single one-shot exception); durable external queue (NATS or equivalent) only under a must-not-lose policy; no bespoke queue microservice
creator: killbus
notes: PHASE = research + design (planning, pre-implementation). MODEL CORRECTED (owner total-silence clarification, 2026-10-30): TWO PROBLEMS. (P1 HEADLINE) The observed symptom is a **10-minute ZERO-request window covering text AND media**, then a catch-up burst; production config **timeoutSeconds: 60** bounds the endpoint worker to <=60 s, so the serial per-endpoint worker CANNOT explain a 10-min zero-request gap (HOL emits at least every 60 s under load) — the silence is an **ABSENCE of SubmitV2 calls**. This rules out endpoint HOL alone (<=60 s), (C) worker wedged >60 s (timeout cap), and (A) album-starvation ALONE (text pushes immediately in the Run loop service.go:352, never via the shared task queue). **Model correction 2 (2026-10-30, owner open-chat observation + Team B ground-fact check):** the silence is *coupled to the official client NOT having the chat open* — client and Budva are SEPARATE sessions, and for channels/large supergroups Telegram does NOT guarantee real-time delivery (gated by chat-open/active state); opening the chat releases a catch-up BURST (difference recovery). Leading causal class = **open-chat-triggered update acquisition (B1a-B1d)** — incl. the DOCUMENTED cross-session passive-update effect for accessible NON-MEMBER channels/supergroups (chatInvitePeek private ones) — with **(B2) Run-loop transient stall**, **(B3) endpoint backlog** (capped <=60 s at timeoutSeconds:60), and **(D) ruleset hot-reload gap** (log signatures 'Ruleset reloaded' / 'Failed to reload' / 'Push submission rejected ... retired' dispatcher.go:128-138) as SECONDARY candidates. Source-verified: Budva makes NO OpenChat/CloseChat/ViewMessages/getChannelDifference calls (passive subscriber); dep zelenin/go-tdlib v0.7.6. Evidence for P1 = the **BOUNDARY-LOCALIZATION EXPERIMENT + one live SIGQUIT dump** (Phase 0p revised, owner-run on box, NOT a timing campaign): record the SOURCE CHAT TYPE (channel/supergroup [any size — no protocol threshold] vs private vs basic-group; joined vs accessible) = the decisive fork; contrast A list-only / B open-after-activity / C client-closed (separate chat types); boundary timestamps S0..W2 + one kill -QUIT 1 while active; interpretation (B0/B1 only after C2 -> upstream acquisition -> 'Budva opens the chat' fix; B0/B1 before C2 but B3-B6 late -> local; A/B/C all recover -> transport/diff recovery or local backpressure; B4 prompt but B5/B6 late -> endpoint worker; B6 prompt but W1 late -> HTTP boundary). FIX DIRECTION shifts from 'raise delivery rate/concurrency/timeout' to **'make Budva an active subscriber'** (OpenChat on ALL ruleset source chats + keep open / poll getChannelDifference per server timeout; native, no new component; **owner requirement: supports EVERY chat type via this one uniform action** — no-op for private/basic-group, real fix for channels/supergroups) — PENDING the experiment (which release boundary governs production). If the box is currently wedged, probe NOW. (P2 SECONDARY) Steady-state per-message delay = serial per-endpoint worker (dispatcher.go:214-237) + cap-256 buffer (dispatcher.go:16,86) + single-attempt sink (delivery.go:133-139) + worker occupied until the HTTP RESPONSE returns (delivery.go:167-172): source-confirmed mechanism, a bounded <=60 s worst-case CONTRIBUTOR, NOT the headline explainer. G/G/1: stability rho=lambda*E[B]<1 (B=actual service time; timeout is only an upper bound, 1/timeout a worst-case service-rate LOWER bound); wait(k)<=requests_ahead*timeout (worst-case upper bound, LINEAR not exponential); a minute-scale delay is CONSISTENT WITH a small backlog (examples 3x60s or tens of 5s) but that is not a production conclusion. The dominant interval (T2-T3 queue wait vs T3-T4 HTTP/ingress) is OPEN from source alone, established by a CONTROLLED TEST (P2), not production data. DESIGN (native/minimal-maintenance, evidence-ordered): Phase 0p GATE(P1) = boundary-localization experiment + one live SIGQUIT dump + owner-supplied source chat type (selects the applicable documented mechanism; fix direction = active subscriber vs Run-loop vs endpoint vs reload). Phase 0 GATE(P2) = in-repo controlled slow-receiver test (reproduce queue-wait growth linearly + bound it under the concurrency/timeout change) — PRODUCTION TIMING COLLECTION IS NOT A GATE (non-reproducible, invasive; Team B P1-02's 'capture a production occurrence' is deliberately replaced by the deterministic test, a documented deviation; R0p is the single sanctioned one-shot production-side forensic for P1). Post-deploy Phase 0b = queue-depth/oldest-age/enqueue->pickup metrics as a VERIFICATION AID (not a gate); payload OccurredAt (service.go:351) gives the receiver arrival-minus-submit for free. Phase 1 = settle contracts (loss/duplicate/ordering/fast-ack/idempotency) + owner-supplied receiver T (one curl -w '%{time_total}' or access log — a single number, NOT a measurement campaign). Phase 2 = timeoutSeconds from receiver T + failure budget + safety margin + loss policy (P95/P99 rule REJECTED: a loss knob under at-most-once; no concrete value set before T + loss policy recorded); concurrency configurable, initial value from the Phase 0 test budget + receiver concurrency ceiling (NOT a preset 4, NOT production-arrival-derived). Loss policy fork: best-effort => Phase 0b metrics + config close it, no new component; must-not-lose => durable queue = off-the-shelf wheel evaluated as a decision (NATS JetStream or Redis Stream, NOT pre-approved by name) + queueSink implementing the existing push.Sink seam + idempotent event_id. EXCLUDED: bespoke in-repo queue microservice, in-budva durable outbox+retry (thickens budva), B' local-outbox+reader, preset concurrency/timeout, production timing collection as a gate, full T1-T4 tracing platform. Team B team-a audit = CHANGES REQUESTED; all corrections applied (evidence boundary; controlled test as gate; rejected P95/P99; no preset 4; G/G/1 stability notation; backlog as example; conditional receiver-throughput; A1 measurable acceptance; citation scope). OPEN OWNER DECISIONS (implementation blockers): (0) **support EVERY source chat type** (owner requirement 2026-10-30: private/basic-group/supergroup/channel) = one **type-agnostic uniform action** — `OpenChat` on every ruleset source chat in Budva's own session (no-op for private/basic-group [global stream, not open-gated]; the real fix for channels/supergroups); source chat type + membership is now **DIAGNOSTIC only** (which documented mechanism explains the coupling; a silence on a private/basic-group = a SEPARATE bug: B1a/B2/D); (1) loss policy best-effort vs must-not-lose; (2) duplicate policy; (3) ordering scope; (4) receiver T + fast-ack/idempotency/concurrency-ceiling contracts. SOURCE-CONFIRM before impl (not design forks): (a) does pinned TDlib auto-poll channel differences while open (else Budva polls getChannelDifference per server timeout); (b) lifecycle (re-open after re-auth, updateChatInaccessible, ruleset hot-reload add/remove -> OpenChat/CloseChat; seams main.go:168 Replace + main.go:183-196 hot-reload); (c) opened-chat ceiling under the production source set.
